path: Sullivan consolidates Republican primary voters; Peltola campaigns on fisheries and rural issues but conserves money. Minor candidates take a few percent.
Low, older, Republican-leaning August turnout; election night shows Sullivan ahead by several points, Peltola close second.
Late absentees narrow the gap slightly; certified result has Sullivan first, so Peltola does not win by 3-6%.
Republican nominee for the post-Greene seat campaigns lightly; Democrat runs underfunded; no third-party candidate clears Georgia's petition bar.
Two-candidate November ballot; midterm mood helps Democrat marginally but district remains roughly Trump +35.
Republican wins around 63-65 percent on November 3; outright majority, no December runoff.
Clyde or Republican nominee coasts; Democrat challenger builds party presence; ballot-access rules keep field to two.
Little campaigning; no outside event changes the safe-red picture.
Republican wins about two-thirds on November 3, clearing 50 percent outright.
Brian Jack runs as comfortable incumbent with Trump backing; little-known Democrat challenges; no minor party qualifies.
Midterm mood trims margin slightly at most.
Jack wins roughly 62-66 percent on November 3, majority in the first round.
Closed GOP primary produces Republican nominee for open seat; Callais aftermath may shift maps or dates, but district stays deep red.
November ballot pits Republican nominee against Democrat and perhaps independents; Republican dominant.
Republican wins well over 50 percent; small risk calendar changes alter what counts as first round.
Carter or Democratic nominee prepares for November amid Callais redraw risk; legislature may reshape district.
Even if lines change, November is a nominee-versus-nominee general with few independents.
Winner clears 50 percent outright; residual risk from calendar restructuring or crowded independent field.
Furlan, having resigned as mayor, leads in Macapá; Clécio and Alcolumbre deploy federal resources and interior mayors.
Polarised two-way race; attacks over administration and alliances; no decisive legal blow.
Close contest; Furlan's capital dominance roughly offsets state machine, outcome near coin-flip, possibly via runoff.
Riedel campaigns as high-approval incumbent with broad centre-right coalition including PL; left candidate nationalises race.
PL mostly stays aligned; agribusiness donors back Riedel; left stuck near a third.
Riedel leads first round, wins outright or is favoured in runoff.
Fagundes claims Bolsonaro mantle; Mendes machine backs Pivetta and trades Senate slots to isolate him.
PL leadership prioritises Senate deals; agribusiness donors lean to Pivetta; polls tight.
Race heads toward runoff; Fagundes competitive but machine advantage favours Pivetta slightly.
Fonteles runs with Lula, Wellington Dias machine and centrão allies; opposition under Ciro Nogueira focuses on Senate.
Fragmented, underfunded opposition; no scandal materialises.
Fonteles wins first round comfortably on October 4.
Vicentinho Júnior seeks centrão and Bolsonarista backing; Dorinha consolidates anti-Barbosa vote with statewide recognition.
Fragmented field; government group weighs which candidate to support; police operations add uncertainty.
Race goes to runoff; Dorinha slightly favoured, Vicentinho one of several viable contenders.
Celina Leão runs as incumbent with Ibaneis machine and Michelle Bolsonaro's PL alignment; left exploits BRB-Master scandal.
Possible rival right candidate splits vote; race heads to runoff.
Right-leaning DF electorate helps Celina in runoff, though scandal keeps it competitive.
Mitidieri runs with state machine and Lula-aligned coalition; PL opposition weighs Senate focus; Valmir's eligibility uncertain.
Opposition fragments or loses Valmir to courts; Mitidieri leads polls.
Mitidieri wins, either first round or in runoff against weaker opposition.
Cameli campaigns as popular outgoing governor; Bittar competes for same right-wing voters; left may run Jorge Viana.
Cameli's legal case does not block him; Bittar trails as second right-wing name.
Cameli tops the poll; Bittar fights for second, not first.
Lira pours mayoral networks and amendment resources into interior; Renan relies on Dantas government and Lula ties.
Bitter two-way contest; possible third candidate from JHC camp splits second votes.
Very close top spot; Lira's mayor network roughly matches Renan's state machine.
Renan and Lira dominate; each voter casts two votes; JHC-aligned third candidate possible.
Renan's group splits second votes; Lira's mayors mobilise interior.
Renan finishes second if Lira edges him, first if not; third-place risk is small.
Braga, Wilson Lima and Alberto Neto compete; Bolsonaro endorses Alberto Neto; Plínio Valério may also run.
Manaus votes heavily for Alberto Neto; Lima's interior machine and Braga's network split the rest.
Three-way contest for two top places; Alberto Neto could be first, second or third.
Braga campaigns with Lula and interior networks; Lima uses state machine; Alberto Neto consolidates right in Manaus.
Right vote split between Lima and Alberto Neto; Braga holds left-centre base.
Braga competitive but not favourite for first; Lima or Alberto Neto likely top.
Rayssa Furlan rides husband's popularity; Randolfe seeks Clécio-Alcolumbre bloc's second vote; Lucas Barreto may split.
Alcolumbre bloc steers votes against Furlan camp, partly toward Randolfe.
Rayssa likely first, Randolfe vying with a third candidate for second.
Rayssa Furlan campaigns on Dr. Furlan's coattails; Alcolumbre-Clécio bloc and Randolfe oppose.
Governor race polarises; Furlan family dominant in Macapá.
Rayssa slightly favoured for first, but Randolfe or bloc candidate could top if Furlan campaign falters.
PT slate runs Rui Costa and Jaques Wagner; Coronel may run separately; ACM Neto's opposition concentrates on one name.
PT dominance splits between Rui and Wagner; opposition name consolidates its voters.
Rui and Wagner close for top; opposition single name a threat for first.
Cid weighs retirement; Camilo Santana's PT shapes slate; Capitão Wagner leads right.
If Cid runs on PT-PSB slate, he competes with PT partner and Wagner.
Real chance Cid does not run; if he runs, left split lets Wagner or partner top.
Wagner leads opposition; PT-PSB coalition fields two names; Girão or PL may run separately.
Right vote partially split; left two names share dominant coalition vote.
Wagner could top, take second, or be pushed to third by two coalition names.
Michelle Bolsonaro confirms Senate run in DF with PL backing; Ibaneis damaged by BRB scandal; left fields Leila and others.
Evangelical and right voters rally behind Michelle; national-ticket switch does not happen.
Michelle tops the DF poll comfortably.
PL runs Michelle and Kicis; Ibaneis competes for second right vote; left may consolidate behind one candidate.
Michelle leads; second place contested among Kicis, Ibaneis and the left name.
Consolidated left candidate or Ibaneis edges Kicis for second in a plausible path.
Casagrande runs as popular ex-governor; Meneguelli surges online; PL fields its own name.
Right vote splits between Meneguelli and PL; Casagrande gathers centre and left second votes.
Casagrande tops poll narrowly over Meneguelli, though anti-Lula mood keeps it close.
Meneguelli seeks right second votes; Contarato runs for left; PL may field rival.
Casagrande leads; Meneguelli competes with Contarato and PL candidate for second.
Meneguelli may take second or even first; split right could drop him to third.
Gracinha runs on popular Caiado government; Gayer seeks Bolsonaro vote; PL-Caiado alliance strained.
Alliance frays; Gayer consolidates bolsonaristas while Gracinha holds centre-right and interior.
Gracinha slightly favoured for first, Gayer close behind.
Gayer runs with Bolsonaro endorsement; Caiado bloc may pair Gracinha with non-PL partner like Vanderlan.
Contest for second among Gayer, Vanderlan and others; Gayer could even top.
Gayer one of two leading names; second is plausible but so are first and third.
Weverton seeks slot via Lula or Brandão deal; Fufuca strong in interior; Brandão may run himself.
Brandão-Dino feud splits slates; Weverton lacks secure machine backing.
Fufuca or Brandão likely top; Weverton competes with Eliziane and others for second.
